display.title: The Shofar of Elul: Wake Up, Sleepers!
display.summary_short: Why the shofar is blown every weekday morning of Elul without a brachah, and how its sound wakes us up to the treasures of Torah and mitzvos.
display.summary_long: A talk from the Tzivos Hashem radio show, given on Rosh Chodesh Elul. Uncle Yossi invites children to come to shul the next morning, when the shofar will be sounded after Shacharis for the first time. On Rosh Hashanah, blowing the shofar is a command from Hashem, so we say the brachah 'lishmoa kol shofar'; in Elul it is only a reminder and a preparation, so no brachah is said. No other mitzvah has a whole month of daily preparation, which shows how special it is. Quoting the Rambam, he explains that the shofar calls 'Wake up, sleepers!' A sleeping person does not notice a fortune lying next to him, or a dangerous animal nearby. The shofar tells us to open our eyes to the treasures of Torah and mitzvos, which bring blessing in this world and the next, and to beware of the yetzer hara's tricks, because aveiros pull us away from Hashem. He ends with the hope that this shofar will lead to the great shofar of Moshiach.
display.lesson: The shofar is a wake-up call: open your eyes to Torah and mitzvos and don't let the yetzer hara lull you to sleep.
